title: Best Dehumidifier for Apartment (2026): Quiet, No-Drain Picks
dek: No floor drain, thin walls, a landlord's carpet and an outlet you share with the AC. These dehumidifiers are built for renting.
description: The best dehumidifier for an apartment or studio: quiet units for shared walls, big-tank or app-alert models that need no drain, and how to dehumidify a rental.
intro: Choosing a **dehumidifier for an apartment** comes with rules a homeowner never thinks about. There's rarely a floor drain to run a hose to, the lease may frown on anything permanent, an overflowing bucket can cost you part of your security deposit, and a droning compressor becomes your neighbor's problem as well as yours. Whether you're in a studio apartment or a two-bedroom, the best unit is the one that works inside those limits.

You're far from alone: about 34.7% of US households rent, according to the 2024 American Community Survey, and most rental units weren't built with a dehumidifier's drainage or power needs in mind. The average studio runs about 472 square feet and the average one-bedroom about 714, so you rarely need a basement-size machine.
We compared quiet ratings, tank sizes, power draw, overflow protection and portability across the models renters actually buy, then matched each to the apartment problem it solves best.
topPicksLead: The **Midea Cube 20** is the best dehumidifier for most apartments: quiet, efficient and fitted with a tank large enough to skip nightly emptying.

products.whyWeLoveIt: It answers the two big apartment questions — where does the water go, and how loud is it? — better than almost anything else in its class. The oversized tank means a trip to the sink every few days instead of every night, and it's quiet enough for a living room.
products.performance: Midea rates it at 20 pints a day for up to 1,500 square feet, which gives real headroom in a studio or one-bedroom. The water collects in the base, which lifts out in one piece. Its Most Efficient badge keeps running costs low, which matters when utilities are on you. For more compact picks, see our [best small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: Eva-Dry EDV-2400 Dehumidifier with Humidistat

products.whyWeLoveIt: If your neighbor has ever knocked on the wall, quiet beats capacity. The EDV-2400's compressor-free thermoelectric design keeps it to a fan's hum that won't carry through drywall, and unlike most minis it has a humidistat, so it backs off once the room reaches your target instead of running all night.
products.performance: As a thermoelectric (Peltier) unit, it removes far less water than a compressor model, so it's best for a single small bedroom or closet rather than a whole apartment. It's Eva-Dry's mid-size model, with more airflow and a bigger tank than the brand's petite EDV-1100, and it shuts off when the tank is full so it can run overnight safely. Like every Peltier design, it works best in warm, humid air. More overnight-friendly options are in our [best dehumidifier for bedroom](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-bedroom/) guide.

blocks.text: Those first two numbers point the same way: most renters need a quiet, compact, single-room machine, not a basement workhorse. The third is a reminder that mold damage in a rental can come out of your deposit, so keeping humidity in check pays off twice.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for apartments

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. We compared manufacturer noise ratings, tank sizes, coverage claims and power draw, checked ENERGY STAR data, and read owner reviews for the issues that matter most to renters: overflows, rattling compressors, flimsy tanks and units that trip breakers.
We weighted noise and no-drain convenience highest, then overflow protection, energy use and how easy each unit is to move when you do.

sections.heading: What to look for in an apartment dehumidifier

items.label: A big tank or smart alerts
items.text: Without a floor drain, a larger tank or an app that warns you before it's full keeps water off the landlord's floor.

items.label: 42 dB or quieter for bedrooms
items.text: Anything around 50 dB is noticeable through drywall. Save the louder units for the living room.

items.label: Auto shutoff when full
items.text: Non-negotiable in a rental. It's the backstop that protects your deposit.

items.label: A circuit check
items.text: If a space heater or window AC shares the circuit, a low-power thermoelectric unit avoids tripped breakers.

items.label: Portability
items.text: You'll move eventually. A compact unit with a handle is easier to pack than a basement-grade box.

sections.heading: How to dehumidify an apartment without a dehumidifier doing all the work

items: **Run the bathroom fan** during showers and for 20 minutes after, and leave the door open once you're done.
**Use the range hood** whenever you boil or simmer, and cover pots.
**Dry laundry in the dryer** or at a laundromat rather than on racks indoors.
**Run your AC** in summer; it removes moisture as it cools.
**Report leaks quickly.** A dripping pipe or failed window seal is the landlord's job to fix, and documenting it protects your deposit.
**Then let the dehumidifier hold the line** at 40–50%, and check it with a hygrometer.

blocks.text: More room-by-room tactics are in our guide on [how to dehumidify a room](/guides/how-to-dehumidify-a-room/).

The **Midea Cube 20** is the best dehumidifier for most apartments, with a quiet rating, a tank big enough to skip daily emptying and enough coverage for a studio or one-bedroom. Choose the **Eva-Dry EDV-2400** when a shared wall makes quiet the top priority, the **hOmeLabs 32-Pint Wi-Fi** if you want tank alerts on your phone, the **Eva-Dry E-333** for a musty closet, and the **Pro Breeze PB-03** if older wiring can't handle a compressor. Own your unit instead? Our [best dehumidifier for condo](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-condo/) guide covers what changes.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for an apartment?
faqs.a: The Midea Cube 20 for most renters. It's rated for up to 1,500 sq ft, holds 3.2 gallons so you empty it less often, and is rated at 42 dB. For a bedroom on a shared wall, the compressor-free Eva-Dry EDV-2400 is the quieter choice, since only a small fan runs.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for a studio apartment?
faqs.a: A 20-pint compressor unit covers a typical studio of around 472 sq ft with room to spare. If humidity is only mildly elevated, a thermoelectric mini can work in a small studio, but it removes far less water.

faqs.q: Do I need a drain to use a dehumidifier in an apartment?
faqs.a: No. Choose a model with a large tank you empty into a sink, or one with app alerts. If your lease allows it, you can also run an included hose into a bathtub or laundry drain. None of our picks need permanent plumbing.

faqs.q: How do you dehumidify an apartment?
faqs.a: Start with ventilation: bathroom fan during and after showers, range hood while cooking, and a dryer instead of indoor drying racks. Run the AC in summer, report leaks to your landlord, and use a dehumidifier to hold 40–50% humidity.

faqs.q: Will an apartment dehumidifier trip my breaker?
faqs.a: A compressor unit typically draws a few hundred watts, which is fine on its own but can tip an older circuit already running a space heater or window AC. In that case, a low-power thermoelectric model like the Pro Breeze PB-03 is safer.

faqs.q: How loud is too loud for an apartment dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Around 50 dB is noticeable in a quiet room and can carry through a shared wall. For overnight use in a bedroom, look for a rating of about 42 dB or lower.
